cards.topic: 01.12. Pledge II — Blanket liens, aggregates, tacit liens
cards.front: What is a blanket lien — which things are excluded?
cards.back:
A non-possessory right of pledge over the pledger's entire present or future property (by a generally worded CONVENTIO PIGNORIS).
• Excluded are things that are not usually pledged individually: household goods and personal effects, clothing, slaves with a special personal function or emotional bond (Ulpian D 20.1.6; Paulus D 20.1.7, Case 159a).
cards.old_front: Was ist ein Generalpfand (blanket lien) — welche Sachen sind ausgenommen?

cards.topic: 01.12. Pledge II — Blanket liens, aggregates, tacit liens
cards.front: Scaevola D 20.1.34.2 (Case 159b): C pledges his entire present and future property to D and then receives a money loan from E. Do the coins fall under the blanket lien?
cards.back:
Scaevola: Yes — once C acquires ownership of the loaned coins, they belong legally and economically to C's property.
• Counter-argument: the loan amount must be repaid, so economically it belongs to the creditor's assets (early Roman AES ALIENUM — “another person's money”).
cards.old_front: Scaevola D 20.1.34.2 (Case 159b): C verpfändet D sein gesamtes gegenwärtiges und künftiges Vermögen und erhält dann von E ein Gelddarlehen. Fallen die Münzen unter das Generalpfand?

cards.topic: 01.12. Pledge II — Blanket liens, aggregates, tacit liens
cards.front: Scaevola D 20.1.34 pr (Case 159b): A pledges his shop (TABERNA) to B; goods come and go and are processed; A dies. In what does B have a right of pledge?
cards.back:
In all goods that were in the shop at A's death.
• TABERNA = aggregate of things (UNIVERSITAS RERUM) with changing contents: right of pledge in every item as soon as A has acquired it and it comes into the shop — even after processing, as long as it stays in the shop.
• If goods leave the shop, the pledge terminates: Scaevola assumes B's consent to the alienation (waiver) — ordinary course of business.
• Only things of which A acquired ownership before his death.
cards.old_front: Scaevola D 20.1.34 pr (Case 159b): A verpfändet seinen Laden (TABERNA) an B; Waren kommen und gehen, werden verarbeitet; A stirbt. Woran hat B ein Pfandrecht?

cards.topic: 01.12. Pledge II — Blanket liens, aggregates, tacit liens
cards.front: What is a PIGNUS TACITUM — is it IUS COGENS?
cards.back:
A right of pledge without an explicit agreement, tacitly inherent in certain contracts (D 20.2) — probably because such clauses were so common.
• Not IUS COGENS but IUS DISPOSITIVUM: the parties could exclude it or limit it to part of the debt (D 20.2.5.1).
cards.old_front: Was ist ein PIGNUS TACITUM — ist es IUS COGENS?

cards.topic: 01.12. Pledge II — Blanket liens, aggregates, tacit liens
cards.front: Residential lease: in what does the landlord have a tacit lien, what does it secure, and what powers does he have?
cards.back:
• In the movables brought in by the tenant (INVECTA ILLATA: furniture, slaves …) that are meant to remain there permanently (Pomponius D 20.2.7.1); likewise for a storehouse, inn, building plot (D 20.2.3).
• Secures all claims arising from the contract: rent and damages for culpable damage (D 20.2.2).
• Requirements: (at least bonitarian) ownership of the tenant + claim.
• Right of seizure by self-help (PERCLUSIO), without an action.
• Tenant: INTERDICTUM DE MIGRANDO for the release of his things when moving out (another's things seized or right of pledge terminated; D 43.32.1 pr).
• Modern: § 1101 ABGB, §§ 559, 561 BGB.
cards.old_front: Wohnungsmiete: Woran hat der Vermieter ein stillschweigendes Pfandrecht, was sichert es, welche Befugnisse hat er?

cards.topic: 01.12. Pledge II — Blanket liens, aggregates, tacit liens
cards.front: Lease of agricultural land: in what does the lessor have a tacit lien — when does it arise?
cards.back:
• In the fruits — but only once the lessee acquires ownership of them by PERCEPTIO; before that they belong to the lessor himself (no pledge in one's own thing, D 50.17.45 pr).
• No right of seizure by self-help: VINDICATIO PIGNORIS.
• The movables the lessee brings onto the land are NOT tacitly pledged — only if expressly pledged; then INTERDICTUM SALVIANUM.
cards.old_front: Pacht landwirtschaftlicher Grundstücke: Woran hat der Verpächter ein stillschweigendes Pfandrecht — wann entsteht es?

cards.topic: 01.12. Pledge II — Blanket liens, aggregates, tacit liens
cards.front: What are “statutory” liens — examples?
cards.back:
Rights of pledge arising directly from statute/the law:
• SC under Marcus Aurelius: whoever gives a loan for the renovation of a building obtains a right of pledge in it (Papinian D 20.2.1).
• Fiscal claims; ward over the guardian's property (Constantine 314 AD); wife to secure the return of the DOS (Justinian 530 AD) — as blanket liens over the entire property.
cards.old_front: Was sind „gesetzliche“ Pfandrechte — Beispiele?

cards.topic: 01.12. Pledge II — Multiple liens and priority
cards.front: Why does Roman law (from the high classical period) allow multiple liens over one thing (example Nike/Europa/Pluto)?
cards.back:
So that the value of a thing can be fully used as security: Nike's silver plate (1.000) secures only Europa's 500; without a further pledge, half of it would remain unused.
• Precursor: conditional rights of pledge — the second arises only when the first terminates; if the first creditor enforces, the condition fails.
cards.old_front: Warum lässt das römische Recht (ab der Hochklassik) mehrfache Verpfändung zu (Beispiel Nike/Europa/Pluto)?

cards.topic: 01.12. Pledge II — Multiple liens and priority
cards.front: What does PRIOR TEMPORE, POTIOR IURE mean — example Nike/Europa/Pluto?
cards.back:
Rank follows the chronological order of creation: the older right of pledge is satisfied first and in full (“first come, first served”).
• Proceeds 1.000: Europa 500, Pluto 400, SUPERFLUUM 100 to Nike.
• Proceeds 800: Europa 500, Pluto only 300.
cards.old_front: Was bedeutet PRIOR TEMPORE, POTIOR IURE — Beispiel Nike/Europa/Pluto?

cards.topic: 01.12. Pledge II — Multiple liens and priority
cards.front: Africanus (Iulianus) D 20.4.9 pr, 9.1 (Case 177): A leases a bath from B starting 1 July and, to secure the lease, pledges and delivers the slave Eros to him; before 1 July he pledges Eros to C for a loan. Whose right of pledge is older?
cards.back:
That of the lessor B — what counts is the earlier conclusion of the contract from which the secured claim arises, not the later start of the lease.
• D 20.4.9.1: a pledge created earlier for a conditional claim ranks before a later one for an unconditional claim (if the condition fails, it terminates — accessoriality; not in the case of a potestative condition).
cards.old_front: Africanus (Iulianus) D 20.4.9 pr, 9.1 (Case 177): A mietet ab 1.7. ein Bad von B und verpfändet und übergibt ihm dafür den Sklaven Eros; vor dem 1.7. verpfändet er Eros an C für ein Darlehen. Wessen Pfandrecht ist älter?

cards.topic: 01.12. Pledge II — Multiple liens and priority
cards.front: Gaius D 20.4.11.2 (Case 178): the lessee P has pledged the fruits and the movables brought onto the land to the lessor V; before that he pledges a thing to K and only afterwards brings it onto the estate. Who has priority?
cards.back: K — V's right of pledge in this thing arises only when it is brought onto the estate, ie after K's.
cards.old_front: Gaius D 20.4.11.2 (Case 178): Pächter P hat dem Verpächter V die Früchte und eingebrachten Sachen verpfändet; vorher verpfändet er eine Sache an K und bringt sie erst danach aufs Gut. Wer hat Vorrang?

cards.topic: 01.12. Pledge II — Multiple liens and priority
cards.front: With which pleas do pledgees assert their rank in court?
cards.back:
• A junior creditor sues (VINDICATIO PIGNORIS) a senior possessor → EXCEPTIO REI SIBI ANTE PIGNERATAE (D 20.4.12 pr).
• Rights of pledge created simultaneously: the possessor is stronger (MELIOR EST CAUSA POSSIDENTIS, D 20.1.10) → EXCEPTIO REI SIBI QUOQUE PIGNERATAE.
• A senior non-possessor sues a junior possessor → the latter: EXCEPTIO REI SIBI QUOQUE PIGNERATAE; the former: REPLICATIO REI SIBI ANTE PIGNERATAE → the senior wins.
cards.old_front: Mit welchen Einreden setzen Pfandgläubiger ihren Rang prozessual durch?

cards.topic: 01.12. Pledge II — Multiple liens and priority
cards.front: Who decides when to sell — what is the IUS OFFERENDI AC SUCCEDENDI?
cards.back:
The first-ranking creditor obtains possession and decides when the thing is sold.
• Junior creditors have the IUS OFFERENDI AC SUCCEDENDI: they can pay off the senior creditor and step into his rank — a claim to the proceeds in the amount paid, in addition to their own claim.
• Eg: Pluto pays Europa 500 → he has rank 1 for 500 + rank 2 for 400 and chooses the most favourable time of sale.
cards.old_front: Wer bestimmt den Verkaufszeitpunkt — was ist das IUS OFFERENDI AC SUCCEDENDI?

cards.topic: 01.12. Pledge II — Multiple liens and priority
cards.front: Tryphoninus D 20.4.20 (Case 172): T has a pledge for a loan; S then lends 50 and receives a pledge in the HYPEROCHA; then T lends a further 40. To whom is the surplus above T's first claim due?
cards.back:
S (for his 50) — under the principle of priority: T's second claim arose after S's right of pledge and has the most junior rank.
• HYPEROCHA = what is left after the FIRST debt owed to T has been paid (when S made his agreement, the second loan did not yet exist).
• S could offer T payment of the first debt and step into the first rank.
• The debtor must disclose existing rights of pledge; fraudulent concealment = CRIMEN STELLIONATUS.
cards.old_front: Tryphoninus D 20.4.20 (Case 172): T hat ein Pfand für ein Darlehen; S leiht danach 50 und erhält ein Pfand an der HYPEROCHA; dann leiht T weitere 40. Wem gebührt der Überschuss über T's erste Forderung?

cards.topic: 01.12. Pledge II — Multiple liens and priority
cards.front: Which exceptions to the principle of priority exist?
cards.back:
a. Statutory privileges: the ward's pledge in the guardian's things bought with the ward's money, the wife's pledge for the DOS, fiscal liens.
b. Right of pledge for a loan to preserve or improve the pledged thing — ranks before older ones because it increases the value (Ulpian D 20.4.5, Case 182).
c. Debt restructuring (conversion): the new creditor steps into the old creditor's rank by agreement (D 20.4.12.8, 12.9) — this does not harm junior creditors, only the person changes.
cards.old_front: Welche Ausnahmen vom Prioritätsprinzip gibt es?

cards.topic: 01.12. Pledge II — Multiple liens and priority
cards.front: Example 39: Brutus has a pledge in Agatha's ship (value 500) for 800. Lysippe lends 400 for the repair; afterwards the ship is worth 1.000. Rank?
cards.back: Lysippe's right of pledge in the repaired ship ranks before Brutus' older one — her loan increased the value of the pledged thing (exception to the principle of priority, Ulpian D 20.4.5).
cards.old_front: Beispiel 39: Brutus hat ein Pfand am Schiff der Agatha (Wert 500) für 800. Lysippe leiht 400 für die Reparatur; das Schiff ist danach 1.000 wert. Rang?

cards.topic: 01.12. Pledge II — Multiple liens and priority
cards.front: [MP June 2023 · Exegesis (24 pts)] Ulpian D 20.4.5 (lib. 3 disputationum): “Interdum posterior potior est priori, ut puta si in rem istam conservandam impensum est quod sequens credidit: veluti si navis fuit obligata et ad armandam eam vel reficiendam ego credidero.” Explain the passage.
cards.back:
Core statement: exception to the principle of priority — sometimes the later pledgee ranks before the earlier one, if his loan was spent on preserving the pledged thing (example: a pledged ship, credit for fitting it out or repairing it).
• Principle: PRIOR TEMPORE, POTIOR IURE — rank by order of creation.
• Reasoning: the later loan preserves or increases the value of the pledged thing; the older creditor benefits from this too → the lender should share in the added value with priority (textbook XII.L.4.b; Example 39).
• Context: multiple liens (since the high classical period), EXCEPTIO/REPLICATIO REI SIBI ANTE PIGNERATAE, IUS OFFERENDI; further exceptions (statutory privileges, debt restructuring); SC of Marcus Aurelius on renovation loans (right of pledge in the building).
• Structure of the exegesis: facts, legal question, decision, reasoning, classification (textbook XV).
cards.old_front: [MP Juni 2023 · Exegese (24 P.)] Ulpian D 20.4.5 (lib. 3 disputationum): „Interdum posterior potior est priori, ut puta si in rem istam conservandam impensum est quod sequens credidit: veluti si navis fuit obligata et ad armandam eam vel reficiendam ego credidero.“ Erkläre die Stelle.

cards.topic: 01.12. Pledge II — Textbook exercises (Ex 57–62, Exercise 3)
cards.front: [Textbook Ex 57] Ago rents an apartment from Bellona; because of rent arrears Bellona impounds two beds in the apartment. Ago pays the rent but, in his anger, vandalises the apartment (damage 200). Can Ago demand the beds back?
cards.back:
No, not yet.
• Bellona has a tacit lien over the movables brought in (INVECTA ILLATA) and was entitled to seize them by self-help.
• The pledge secures ALL claims arising from the lease — including the damages of 200 for culpable damage.
• Only after payment of the 200 does the right of pledge terminate; then INTERDICTUM DE MIGRANDO.
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Ex 57] Ago mietet von Bellona eine Wohnung; wegen Mietrückstands pfändet Bellona zwei Betten in der Wohnung. Ago zahlt die Miete, demoliert aber aus Wut die Wohnung (Schaden 200). Kann Ago die Betten zurückverlangen?

cards.topic: 01.12. Pledge II — Textbook exercises (Ex 57–62, Exercise 3)
cards.front: [Textbook Ex 58] Nike pledges her leased pottery workshop to her lender Orion (including a kiln built into the wall; both belong to Pius). At maturity the workshop contains three potter's wheels belonging to Nike, clay, greenware and fired vessels — five amphorae of which are sold to Quinta but not yet delivered — and three flower pots belonging to Rhianos, there for repair. In what does Orion have a right of pledge?
cards.back:
• Workshop and kiln (firmly built in — part of the building, SUPERFICIES SOLO CEDIT): no pledge — owned by Pius, Nike has no power of disposal.
• The workshop as TABERNA/aggregate of things (Scaevola D 20.1.34 pr): pledge in everything that belongs to Nike and is located in it — potter's wheels, clay, greenware, fired vessels.
• Also in the amphorae sold to Quinta: without delivery still Nike's property.
• Not in Rhianos' flower pots (another's property).
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Ex 58] Nike verpfändet ihrem Darlehensgeber Orion ihre gepachtete Töpferwerkstatt (samt in die Wand eingebautem Brennofen, beides gehört Pius). Bei Fälligkeit sind dort drei Töpferscheiben Nikes, Ton, Rohware und gebrannte Gefäße — fünf Amphoren davon an Quinta verkauft, aber nicht geliefert — sowie drei Blumentöpfe des Rhianos zur Reparatur. Woran hat Orion ein Pfandrecht?

cards.topic: 01.12. Pledge II — Textbook exercises (Ex 57–62, Exercise 3)
cards.front: [Textbook Ex 59] Ismene pledges “her forest” to Ramses (100.000), later to Juno (20.000). Ramses has the forest auctioned for 110.000. Distribution? Variant: Ismene fells the trees and builds a ship — right of pledge in the ship?
cards.back:
Distribution under PRIOR TEMPORE, POTIOR IURE: Ramses 100.000, Juno 10.000 (remaining claim of 10.000 unsecured), no SUPERFLUUM for Ismene. Juno claims her share with the ACTIO UTILIS.
Variant: No — Paulus (Cassius) D 13.7.18.3: the ship is an ALIUD (SPECIFICATIO); the pledge in the “forest” terminates when the forest ceases to exist; different only if whatever is made from it was expressly pledged as well.
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Ex 59] Ismene verpfändet „ihren Wald“ an Ramses (100.000), später an Juno (20.000). Ramses lässt den Wald um 110.000 versteigern. Verteilung? Variante: Ismene fällt die Bäume und baut ein Schiff — Pfandrecht am Schiff?

cards.topic: 01.12. Pledge II — Textbook exercises (Ex 57–62, Exercise 3)
cards.front: [Textbook Ex 60] Cato grants Daphne a non-possessory pledge in his slave Pomona for a loan; later he pledges and delivers Pomona to Eros for a purchase-price claim. Cato does not pay. Can Daphne demand that Pomona be handed over? What can Eros do?
cards.back:
• Daphne has the senior rank → VINDICATIO PIGNORIS against Eros; Eros: EXCEPTIO REI SIBI QUOQUE PIGNERATAE; Daphne: REPLICATIO REI SIBI ANTE PIGNERATAE → Daphne wins.
• Eros: IUS OFFERENDI AC SUCCEDENDI — he pays Daphne's claim and steps into her first rank; he then decides on the enforcement himself.
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Ex 60] Cato bestellt Daphne für ein Darlehen ein besitzloses Pfand an seiner Sklavin Pomona; später verpfändet und übergibt er Pomona an Eros für eine Kaufpreisforderung. Cato zahlt nicht. Kann Daphne Pomona herausverlangen? Was kann Eros tun?

cards.topic: 01.12. Pledge II — Textbook exercises (Ex 57–62, Exercise 3)
cards.front: [Textbook Ex 61] Gaia borrows 1.000 each from Hermes and Japyx and pledges a plot of land to both simultaneously; Hermes takes possession of it. At maturity Japyx wants to sell immediately, Hermes wants to wait. (a) Can Japyx demand possession from Hermes? (b) What can Japyx do?
cards.back:
(a) No — rights of pledge created simultaneously: MELIOR EST CAUSA POSSIDENTIS; Hermes defeats the VINDICATIO PIGNORIS with the EXCEPTIO REI SIBI QUOQUE PIGNERATAE.
(b) Japyx can pay off Hermes' claim (IUS OFFERENDI AC SUCCEDENDI) and thus take over his position, then enforce himself.
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Ex 61] Gaia leiht sich von Hermes und Japyx je 1.000 und verpfändet beiden gleichzeitig ein Grundstück; Hermes nimmt es in Besitz. Bei Fälligkeit will Japyx sofort verkaufen, Hermes warten. (a) Kann Japyx von Hermes den Besitz verlangen? (b) Was kann Japyx tun?

cards.topic: 01.12. Pledge II — Textbook exercises (Ex 57–62, Exercise 3)
cards.front: [Textbook Ex 62] Julius pledges his house on 1 March to Kassandra (500), on 1 May to Leo (200, voyage by ship), on 1 August to Melitta, who lends him 400 for a complete refurbishment of the house. Proceeds after enforcement 1.000 — distribution?
cards.back:
Melitta 400 (priority despite the most recent creation: loan for the preservation/improvement of the pledged thing, Ulpian D 20.4.5), then Kassandra 500, then Leo 100 (the rest of his 200 unsecured).
• Without the exception: Kassandra 500, Leo 200, Melitta 300.
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Ex 62] Julius verpfändet sein Haus am 1.3. an Kassandra (500), am 1.5. an Leo (200, Schiffsreise), am 1.8. an Melitta, die ihm 400 für eine Generalsanierung des Hauses leiht. Erlös nach Verwertung 1.000 — Verteilung?

cards.topic: 01.12. Pledge II — Textbook exercises (Ex 57–62, Exercise 3)
cards.front: [Textbook Exercise 3, ch. XIII] On 1 January Niobe borrows 100 from Thoas (non-possessory pledge in her silver plate) and on 1 May 200 from Crassus, to whom she hands over the plate as a pledge. She falls behind with the instalments; Thoas wants to enforce. What can Thoas do, and what is Crassus' position?
cards.back:
• Thoas' right of pledge: claim (100) + Niobe's ownership + CONVENTIO PIGNORIS (delivery unnecessary) → valid, rank 1.
• Crassus: valid possessory pledge, rank 2 (PRIOR TEMPORE, POTIOR IURE).
• Thoas: VINDICATIO PIGNORIS against Crassus; he overcomes Crassus' EXCEPTIO REI SIBI QUOQUE PIGNERATAE with the REPLICATIO REI SIBI ANTE PIGNERATAE.
• Crassus can pay Thoas off (IUS OFFERENDI AC SUCCEDENDI) or, upon enforcement, receives the surplus after Thoas (ACTIO UTILIS).
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Exercise 3, Kap. XIII] Niobe leiht am 1.1. von Thoas 100 (besitzloses Pfand an ihrem Silberteller) und am 1.5. von Crassus 200, dem sie den Teller als Pfand übergibt. Sie gerät mit den Raten in Rückstand; Thoas will verwerten. Was kann Thoas tun, wie steht Crassus?
